Duplicate heartbeats from orchestrator job retries causing persistent 429s during nightly snapshot imports

Issue summary: DataRidge reports recurring 429 responses across many workers during their nightly snapshot import (23:00-00:30 UTC). Requests originate from their Dedicated pool; the symptoms began after a recent orchestrator rollout and persist nightly.

Impact: Import jobs are failing/retrying, causing duplicate processing and delayed ingestion; customer reports 15-25% of batch workers receiving 429s, import duration doubled, downstream analytics delayed. No data loss reported but SLA breaches for import completion window.

Environment: prod-us-west, Dedicated pool: dp-dataridge-01, region us-west, models used for enrichment: embed-large-v2 and reranker-mini.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Kick off standard nightly snapshot job (orchestrator v2.3.1) across 200 worker pods.
2) Observe periodic 429 responses during the first 10 minutes of the job, often concurrent with coordinator retries.
3) Job retries immediately and creates more outbound connections, leading to sustained 429s for 10-20 minutes.

Observed logs and sample traces:
- "rate_limiter=reject action=throttle tenant=dridge tokens=0 path=/v1/generate status=429 source=edge-12"
- Orchestrator stderr: "Heartbeat send failed, will retry in 2s (attempt 3)"
- Edge proxy logs show repeated POSTs from the same source IP within 1s windows, differing only by ephemeral request-id.

Customer-provided attachments: request-rate heatmap (peaks at 12k rps), coordinator retry logs, and job config.

Immediate asks from customer: guidance on how to avoid 429s during nightly imports and whether Dedicated pool limits can be temporarily increased or exempted for scheduled jobs.
2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged. Opening investigation and requested job config and sample worker logs from customer.
2026-03-10 10:03 - DataRidge (customer): Sent job config and compressed logs; noted that the orchestrator rollout to v2.3.1 coincided with the start of the problem.
2026-03-10 14:45 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Initial hypothesis: orchestrator retry storm + healthcheck/heartbeat pings were being counted against tenant quota. Requested sample edge-proxy traces and rate-limiter counters (shard metrics).
2026-03-11 02:21 - SRE (automation): Pulled rate-limiter shard metrics for dp-dataridge-01: burst_window_tokens exhausted repeatedly between 23:01-23:12 UTC. Increase in connections from orchestrator coordinator host ip-10-4-22-93 at same timestamps.
2026-03-11 08:37 - Eng (ingest-orch): Reproduced orchestration behavior in staging with a 50-worker job configured to aggressively retry heartbeats; observed duplicate heartbeat POSTs when backoff misapplies jitter leading to near-synchronous retries.
2026-03-12 11:18 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation: exempted healthcheck/heartbeat route from tenant token accounting for dp-dataridge-01 and raised burst pool cap by 20% for nightly window. Customer to verify tonight. Follow-up PR created to dedupe heartbeats at source.
2026-03-12 16:02 - DataRidge (customer): Confirmed a dramatic reduction in 429s during the nightly import after mitigation; import completed within expected window. Asking for permanent solution and rollback safety window.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Noted success; scheduling post-mortem and permanent fix path with Eng.
Rate-limiter findings: shard token depletion pattern consistent with many short-lived concurrent connections; accounting shows healthcheck-originating requests counted against tenant quota.
Orchestrator behavior: v2.3.1 introduced a retry coordinator that lacks sufficient jitter and dedupe when multiple workers detect transient failures, producing synchronized retry waves.
Edge-proxy: HTTP/2 connection reuse caused multiple logical streams to appear as separate request-ids at rate-limiter layer, exacerbating token accounting (duplicate counts).
Quick reproducer in staging: enabled aggressive retry config and observed 3x token consumption within 30s vs prior behavior; fixed by adding jitter and idempotency header in test run.
Dashboards consulted: /dashboards/rate-limiter/tokens-by-tenant, /dashboards/edge/proxy-connections, incident log:INC-2026-03-11-01
Mitigation applied 2026-03-12: (1) exempted heartbeat/healthcheck endpoints from tenant token accounting for dp-dataridge-01 during 22:50-00:30 UTC nightly window, (2) temporarily increased dedicated burst pool cap by 20% for the nightly window, (3) merged and rolled out PR github.com/redwood-inference/ingest-orch/pull/412 that adds jitter + dedupe key to orchestrator heartbeats. Customer validated reduction in 429s and normal import completion.

Permanent follow-ups (internal tasks): INT-821 to add global rate-limiter rule to ignore ephemeral healthcheck tokens where a valid service-account header is present; INT-822 to add a configurable scheduled burst pool option for Dedicated customers; ENG task to monitor for regressions over the next two nightly runs. Support to coordinate rollback plan and update customer runbook.
